To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

bias amplification can be caused by adding group fixed effects, that the bias unmasking effect can occur in some settings, and that adding bias decomposition information to sensitivity analysis displays can help practitioners think through these issues.
1) bias amplification can occur when using fixed effects and 2) bias unmasking can occur when conditioning on certain covariate combinations

(1) conditioning on certain covariate groups can increase omitted variable bias, (2) bias amplification can occur even when conditioning on a group fixed effect, and (3) bias amplification is not the only way that conditioning on certain groups can increase bias; bias unmasking is another way that conditioning on groups can lead to increased bias.
In summary, our research is concerned with

understanding how the use of observed covariates can lead to bias in observational studies, and we hope our results will help practitioners think more carefully about the use of observed and unobserved covariates in observational studies.
how to think about the effects of conditioning on covariates in the presence of unobserved confounders and how to use graphical sensitivity analyses to think through these problems in practice.
the potential for bias to increase in observational studies when conditioning on certain covariate sets, which can occur even when conditioning on a large number of covariates.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
conditioning on covariates can be beneficial, harmful, or even harmful and beneficial at the same time.
the potential for bias due to conditioning on certain covariate combinations should not be ignored.
the use of instruments or group fixed effects may lead to bias amplifcation and/or bias unmasking.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
bias amplification is a real and important phenomenon, but bias unmasking is an even more important phenomenon, and it can be more difficult to detect and avoid.
conditioning on observable covariate can increase bias and the mechanism for this is not necessarily the same as the mechanism for bias due to an omitted variable.
bias amplification and unmasking are not rare occurrences and can be a serious threat to causal inference in observational studies.
The main takeaway from our work is that
practitioners should be aware that conditioning on certain observable covariates can increase bias, and that the mechanisms underlying this bias increase are not always obvious.
researchers should not assume that conditioning on covariates is always beneficial.
conditioning on observable covariate can lead to bias, and the bias can be amplified or even unmasked.
